The Winds Shift in Manila

And then, the House of Representatives gave the nation a symbol that could not be ignored: during budget deliberations, Sara Duterte was addressed as “Her Excellency.” The OVP budget sailed smoothly through both the House and the Senate—without the toxic grandstanding, sabotage, or hostility that once defined every peso allocated to her office.

This was not mere courtesy. It was submission. It was lawmakers acknowledging the end of the demolition drive against the Dutertes. The balance of fear in Congress had shifted. The crosshairs now fixed firmly on Malacañang.

Romualdez and Co: The Fall of the Shields

The first great shield of Marcos power collapsed with the resignation of House Speaker Martin Romualdez. He tried to mask his exit as a noble gesture—“service, not retreat.” In truth, he was forced to jump before the scandal consumed him. The allegations tied to massive flood-control projects had eroded his credibility, and the pressure became untenable.

Soon after, another domino fell. Zaldy Co, Romualdez’s ally and a trusted operator, resigned. His name exploded across the nation’s headlines after MSgt Orly Regala Guteza testified before the Senate. Guteza’s testimony was devastating: suitcases stuffed with cash, delivered multiple times to Co’s residence at Horizon Towers, to Romualdez’s McKinley Street address, and finally—to a house on Aguada Street, just minutes from Malacañang’s gate.

The details were too specific to ignore. Guteza spoke of how deliveries were trimmed—forty-six luggages taken, thirty-five left behind—implying a corrupt chain of command and selective distribution. The demolition front that once targeted Duterte has disintegrated into a chaotic retreat.

#LadyRadar whispers as the cooler seasons come in, tears and curiosities await your visit to the theater this September, with stories that bridge fantasy and reality.

Theater Group Asia opens this well-loved romance at the Samsung Performing Arts Theater on September 3. Their stellar cast includes Morisette in her theatrical debut, Celeste Legaspi, Rody Vera, Sheena Belarmino, Benedix Ramos, and Laurence Mossman.

❤️‍🩹"Tagay Para Sa Ex."
Boxstage Manila's season opener brings out the stories of love and heartache that only come up after you've had a drink, written and directed by Dudz Teraña. They run until September 5 at the FEU Black Box.

👥"Subversive Lives."
Based on Susan and Nathan Gilbert Quimpo' "Subversive Lives: A Family Memoir of the Marcos Years", Arete's season opener follows the Quimpo family during the Martial Law era. They will show until September 6 at the Doreen Black Box, Arete.

🩰"1001 Nights."
Ballet Philippines takes their dancers into a magical Arabian tale for 3 days only, from September 11 to 13 at Solaire. This show is definitely one the kids wouldn't wanna miss.

🎸"Muli."
Another original OPM musical by Charissa Pammit, creator of "Sa Wakas", opens September 11 at the Globe Auditorium. Featuring Janine Teñoso in her musical debut alongside Gawa Urian Awardee Kakki Teodoro, playing a mother and daughter duo.

🐴"A Midsummer Night's Dream."
Repertory Theater stages this Shakespeare classic at St. Scholastica College Manila, with an ensemble set to bring us a show full of laughter, romance, and magic. They run from September 12 to 27 only.

💃🏽"Bongga Ka Day!"
Full House Theater gives us another jukebox musical, with the iconic music of the band Hotdog. Atasha Mulach is set to play Annie Batungbakal, a 'dispatsadora' by day and a disco queen by night. Opening September 18 at the Newport Theater.

🕯️"Sayaw ng mga Ilaw."
Tanghalanag Pilipino's first official show for their 40th season is Juan Ekis' stage adaptation of Cheeno Marlo Sayuno's well-loved children's short story. They open September 18 at the Tanghalang Ignacio Gimenez.

💊"The Effect."
C.A.S.T. PH sets the stage for Lucy Prebble's play following two people who fall in love at, of all places, a clinical drug trial, throwing the trial off-course. Opens September 19 at the Doreen Blackbox, Areté.

🪖"Bantayog."
SceneChange's twin-playbill staged reading follows close-to-home stories on Martial Law. Their first weekend September 19 to 20 shows "Villa" by Chilean writer Guillermo Calderon, while for their second weekend September 26 to 27, Guelan Varela-Luarca adapts Lualhati Bautista's novel "Desaparesidos" for the stage. They will be showing at the Power Mac Center Spotlight Blackbox.

🚪"Silid 13."
Rosa Artes' maiden show by Joanne Caringal is a psychological drama about a man facing 13 closed-off rooms deep within his mind that he has ignored for years. For two days only, September 26 and 27, at the Sta Rosa Elementary School, Laguna.

⛈️"Ambon, Ulan, Baha."
Staging at the Metropolitan Theater from September 26 to 27 only, and starring CJ Navato and Thea Astley, this very timely rerun of the musical written by Frank G. Rivera returns home to where it first played.

👠"Cinderella."
Repertory Theater presents this well-loved classic fairytale with three alternating Cinderellas—Katie Bradshaw, Ornella Brianna, and Julia Santiago. Take the time to choose your princess, as their run lasts until December 13 at REP Eastwood.
